answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via time-locked fidelity bonds. Each agent locks collateral in an on-chain escrow for a fixed unbonding window, binding its key to a slashable economic signal. Because identities cannot flare and vanish like a comet at zero cost, attackers must freeze real funds and risk confiscation per identity, whether run on cheap hosts or a marble trading floor. However, wealthy actors can still fund many keys while pricing out uncapitalized agents.
